chunks: They had almost led you away from what has been revealed to you, that you may invent things about Us besides those revealed, when they would have taken you as friend.

key_terms.يَفْتِنُونَكَ: They would lead you astray/test you

ai.seo_question: What did the disbelievers want the Prophet to do with the revelation?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the Prophet's absolute fidelity (Ismah) against the subtle political and social pressures of the Quraysh, who sought to co-opt him as a 'khalil' (close friend/ally) if he compromised the purity of revelation. The term 'khalil' implies a deep, almost familial bond, highlighting that the disbelievers desired not just a messenger, but a partner in their own worldly interests, a test the Prophet successfully navigated by remaining distinct from their idolatrous culture.
